    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
\), there is a canonical isomorphism
\[
\mathrm{H}^i({}_{\mathrm{HW}}(M))(-i)
 \cong{}_{\mathrm{HW}}\bigl(\mathrm{H}^i(M)(-i)\bigr).
\]
After undoing the internal twist, we abbreviate this as
\(\mathrm{H}^i({}_{\mathrm{HW}}(M))\cong{}_{\mathrm{HW}}(\mathrm{H}^i(M))\).
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Set \(A={}_{\mathrm{HW}}(M)\). Since \(A\) is Hodge--Witt, each
\(\mathrm{H}^j(A)\) is concentrated in internal degree \(-j\). Its ordinary
cohomology filtration therefore splits by internal degree, so
\(\mathrm{H}^i(A)[-i]\) is a direct summand of \(A\). Let \(Q\) be the
cokernel of the resulting monomorphism
\(\mathrm{H}^i(A)[-i]\hookrightarrow M\) in \( 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}              
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.11, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}             
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.08, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
\). The connecting map
\(\mathrm{H}^{i-1}(Q)\to\mathrm{H}^i(A)\) vanishes: its source is generated in
internal degree \(1-i\), whereas its target is concentrated in degree
\(-i\). Hence \(\mathrm{H}^i(A)\to\mathrm{H}^i(M)\) is injective, with Hodge--Witt
image.

We claim that \({}_{\mathrm{HW}}(X)=0\) implies
\({}_{\mathrm{HW}}(\mathrm{H}^i(X)(-i))=0\) for every \(i\). Put
\(S={}_{\mathrm{HW}}(\mathrm{H}^i(X)(-i))\). Through the canonical monomorphism
\(\mathrm{H}^i(X)[-i]\hookrightarrow\tau_{\geqslant i}X\), regard
\(S(i)[-i]\) as a subobject of \(\tau_{\geqslant i}X\), and let
\(N\subseteq X\) be its inverse image. There is an exact sequence
\(0\to\tau_{\leqslant i-1}X\to N\to S(i)[-i]\to0\) in \( 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}              
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.11, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}             
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.08, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
\).
The left term is supported in internal degrees at least \(1-i\), while
the right term is supported in degree \(-i\). Thus \(N\) is cut at \(\{-i\}\), and
\Cref{D_c^b(R-Cut-I)} splits the sequence by internal degree.
Hence \(S(i)[-i]\) is a Hodge--Witt subobject of \(X\), forcing
\(S=0\).

Now apply the claim to \(X=M/A\), for which \({}_{\mathrm{HW}}(X)=0\). The
image of any Hodge--Witt subobject of \(\mathrm{H}^i(M)(-i)\) in
\(\mathrm{H}^i(X)(-i)\) is again Hodge--Witt and hence zero. It is therefore
contained in \(\mathrm{H}^i(A)(-i)\); the reverse inclusion was proved above.
This gives the asserted canonical isomorphism.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{survie du coeur}
Let \(M\in D_c^b(R)\), and consider the slope spectral sequence
\[
E_1^{i,j}=\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\Longrightarrow\mathrm{H}^{i+j}(\mathrm{Tot}(M)).
\]

{\rm (1)} One has
\[
B_\infty^{i,j}\subseteq F^\infty B\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i
\subseteq V^{-\infty}Z\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i
\subseteq Z_\infty^{i,j}.
\]

{\rm (2)} Under the canonical identification
\[
\mathrm{Fil}^j\mathrm{H}^{i+j}(\mathrm{Tot}(M))/\mathrm{Fil}^{j-1}\mathrm{H}^{i+j}(\mathrm{Tot}(M))
 \cong Z_\infty^{i,j}/B_\infty^{i,j},
\]
every torsion class in
\(V^{-\infty}Z\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i/B_\infty^{i,j}\) lifts to a torsion class in
\(\mathrm{Fil}^j\mathrm{H}^{i+j}(\mathrm{Tot}(M))\).
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
Let \(f:X^\bullet\to Y^\bullet\) be a morphism of complexes in an
abelian category. If \(f^i\) is surjective and \(f^{i+1}\) is
injective, then \(\mathrm{H}^i(f)\) is surjective and
\(\mathrm{H}^{i+1}(f)\) is injective.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Every cycle in \(Y^i\) lifts to \(X^i\), and the lift is a cycle
because \(f^{i+1}\) is injective. This proves surjectivity on \(\mathrm{H}^i\).
If a cycle in \(X^{i+1}\) maps to a boundary, lift a primitive through
the surjection \(f^i\); injectivity of \(f^{i+1}\) then shows that the
original cycle is a boundary.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Put \(n=i+j\) and \(X=\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n-1}M\). Since ordinary and
diagonal truncations commute, \(X\to M\) induces the inclusion
\[
E_1^{i,j}(X)=F^\infty B\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i
 \hookrightarrow E_1^{i,j}(M)=\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i,
\]
and is an isomorphism in total degrees below \(n\). Repeated application
of the preceding lemma gives the same comparison on every page, with
injectivity in total degree \(n\). Every boundary entering \((i,j)\)
therefore lifts from \(X\), proving
\(B_\infty^{i,j}\subseteq F^\infty B\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\).
The inclusion \(F^\infty B\subseteq V^{-\infty}Z\) follows from
\(dV^rF^a d=0\) for \(a,r\geqslant0\).

For the last inclusion, consider the radical filtration on \( 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}              
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.11, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}             
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.08, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
\)
\[
T^a=0\quad(a<-1),\qquad T^{-1}={}_{\mathrm{HW}},\qquad
T^a=\mathrm{id}\quad(a\geqslant0).
\]
Its only nonformal orthogonality is
\(\mathrm{Hom}_{ 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}              
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.11, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}             
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.08, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
}({}_{\mathrm{HW}}(A),B/{}_{\mathrm{HW}}(B))=0\): the image would be a
Hodge--Witt subobject of \(B/{}_{\mathrm{HW}}(B)\). Write
\(\widehat\tau_{\leqslant a}\) for the associated truncation. By construction,
\[
\widetilde{\mathrm{H}}^q(\widehat\tau_{\leqslant a}M)\cong
\begin{cases}
\widetilde{\mathrm{H}}^q(M),&q\leqslant a,\\
{}_{\mathrm{HW}}(\widetilde{\mathrm{H}}^{a+1}(M)),&q=a+1,\\
0,&q>a+1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(M'=\widehat\tau_{\leqslant n-1}M\), this formula and
\Cref{HW of cohomology equals cohomology of HW} give
\[
E_1^{i,j}(M')=V^{-\infty}Z\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i
 \hookrightarrow E_1^{i,j}(M),\qquad
E_1^{\ell,k}(M')=0\quad(k+\ell>n).
\]
All outgoing differentials at \((i,j)\) for \(M'\) have zero target,
so functoriality gives \(V^{-\infty}Z\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\subseteq Z_\infty^{i,j}\),
completing (1).

For (2), first note that every class in
\(F^\infty B\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i/B_\infty^{i,j}\) has a torsion lift in
\(\mathrm{Fil}^j\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} M)\). Indeed, this quotient is the image of
\(E_\infty^{i,j}(X)\), since \(X\) has no \(E_1\)-terms in total
degrees above \(n\). The group \(\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} X)\) is torsion by
\Cref{Totsubquo}(1) and \Cref{Basic Vanishing}(1).

Now choose \(x\in V^{-\infty}Z\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\) representing the given
torsion class \(\bar x\). Put
\[
A=\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n-1}(\tau_{\leqslant j}M),\qquad
M'=\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n}(\tau_{\leqslant j}M),\qquad
D=\widetilde{\mathrm{H}}^n(\tau_{\leqslant j}M),\quad C=D[-n].
\]
The triangle \(A\to M'\to C\to A[1]\) induces, in bidegree \((i,j)\),
the quotient map
\[
\mathrm{H}^j(M')^i=\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\longrightarrow
\mathrm{H}^j(C)^i=\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i/F^\infty B\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i.
\]
Let \(x_C\) be the image of \(x\). It is torsion because
\(p^a\bar x=0\) implies \(p^ax\in B_\infty^{i,j}\subseteq F^\infty B\).
Moreover, \(B_\infty^{i,j}(C)=0\), since the \(E_1\)-page of \(C\)
is supported in total degrees \(n\) and \(n+1\).

Apply the finite-torsion sequence
\(0\to t^1(D)\to D\to t^0(D)\to0\).
By \Cref{description of finite torsion object}(2),(3), the stable cycles
of \(t^0(D)[-n]\) in total degree \(n\) are torsion free. Thus \(x_C\)
maps to zero there and lifts to \(\mathrm{H}^j(t^1(D)[-n])^i\).
By part (1) of the same theorem, \(t^1(D)\) splits into shifts of
finite-length Dieudonn\'e modules. Its slope spectral sequence
therefore degenerates at \(E_1\), giving a torsion class
\(u\in\mathrm{Fil}^j\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} C)\) representing \(x_C\).

Since \(\mathrm{H}^{n+1}(\mathrm{Tot} A)=0\), lift \(u\) to
\(v\in\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} M')\). The lift is torsion since \(u\) and
\(\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} A)\) are torsion, the latter by
\Cref{Totsubquo}(1) and \Cref{Basic Vanishing}(1).
As \(M'\to M\) factors through \(\tau_{\leqslant j}M\), its image lies
in \(\mathrm{Fil}^j\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} M)\) and represents \(\bar x\) modulo
\(F^\infty B\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i/B_\infty^{i,j}\).
Correcting it by a torsion lift constructed above gives a torsion
lift of \(\bar x\).
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{Filtration of torsion}
Let \(M\in D^{b}_{c}(R)\).

{\rm (1)} The exotic \(1\)-torsion of \(M\) in degree \(i\) is the
image of
\[
\mathrm{H}^1\bigl(\mathrm{Tot}(\widetilde\mathrm{H}^{i-1}(M))\bigr)
 \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(\mathrm{Tot}(M)).
\]

{\rm (2)} The finite total torsion of \(M\) in degree \(i\) is
\[
\mathrm{H}^0\bigl(\mathrm{Tot}(t^0(\widetilde\mathrm{H}^i(M)))\bigr).
\]

{\rm (3)} The exotic \(0\)-torsion of \(M\) in degree \(i\) is the
torsion subgroup of
\[
\mathrm{H}^0\bigl(\mathrm{Tot}(t^1(\widetilde\mathrm{H}^i(M)))\bigr).
\]
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{When one of the differential is zero}
Let \(M\in D^b_c(R)\), and suppose that
\(d:\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\to\mathrm{H}^j(M)^{i+1}\) is zero.

{\rm (1)} The quotient of \(\mathrm{H}^{i+j}(\mathrm{Tot}(M))\) by its exotic
\(1\)-torsion admits a canonical decomposition
\(\mathrm{H}^{\leqslant i}\oplus\mathrm{H}^{>i}\).

{\rm (2)} In the slope spectral sequence, the differentials
\[
E_r^{k,l}\longrightarrow E_r^{k+r,l-r+1}
\]
vanish whenever \(k+l=i+j\) and \(i-r<k\leqslant i\).
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Put \(n=i+j\) and \(C=\widetilde{\mathrm{H}}^n(M)[-n]\). Since ordinary and diagonal
truncations commute,
\[
\mathrm{H}^l(C)=
\frac{\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n-l}\mathrm{H}^l(M)}
     {\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n-l-1}\mathrm{H}^l(M)}.
\]
This module is supported in internal degrees \(n-l\) and \(n-l+1\).
The differential from internal degree \(i\) to \(i+1\) can be
nonzero only for \(l=j\), when it vanishes by hypothesis. Thus \(C\) is cut at \(\{i\}\). By
\Cref{D_c^b(R-Cut-I)}, it splits canonically as
\(C=C_{\leqslant i}\oplus C_{>i}\), with the two summands supported
in the indicated internal degrees.

By \Cref{Totsubquo}(1), the quotient of \(\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} M)\) by its
exotic \(1\)-torsion is canonically \(\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} C)\). The splitting
of \(C\) therefore proves (1), with
\(\mathrm{H}^{\leqslant i}=\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} C_{\leqslant i})\) and
\(\mathrm{H}^{>i}=\mathrm{H}^n(\mathrm{Tot} C_{>i})\).

For (2), set \(X=\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n}M\) and
\(A=\widetilde{\tau}_{\leqslant n-1}M\), so that
\(A\to X\to C\to A[1]\) is a distinguished triangle.
On the \(E_1\)-page, both maps \(X\to M\) and \(X\to C\) are
surjective in total degree \(n\) and injective in total degree
\(n+1\): for the first this follows from the truncation formula,
and for the second from \(\mathrm{H}^l(A)^k=0\) when \(k+l>n\).
The comparison lemma preceding the proof of \Cref{survie du coeur}
propagates these properties to every page.

If \(i-r<k\leqslant i\), the differential \(d_r\) crosses the cut
and hence vanishes for \(C\). Given a class in \(E_r^{k,l}(M)\), lift it to
\(E_r^{k,l}(X)\). Its differential maps to zero for \(C\), hence
is zero by injectivity in total degree \(n+1\). Its image for
\(M\) is therefore zero as well, proving (2).
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{Hodge Witt in degree r}
An object \(M\in D_c^b(R)\) is Hodge--Witt in degree \(r\) if
\(d:\mathrm{H}^j(M)^i\to\mathrm{H}^j(M)^{i+1}\) vanishes whenever \(i+j=r\).
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{Tot torsion definition}
Let \(M\in 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\,

    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{

    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}}

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
\).

{\rm (1)} The object \(M\) is without \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-torsion if
\(\mathrm{H}^*(\mathrm{Tot}(M))\) is torsion free.

{\rm (2)} It is \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-torsion if \(\mathrm{H}^*(\mathrm{Tot}(M))\) is torsion.

{\rm (3)} It is \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-\(0\)-torsion if it is \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-torsion and
\(\mathrm{H}^1(\mathrm{Tot}(M))=0\); it is \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-\(1\)-torsion if it is
\(\mathrm{Tot}\)-torsion and \(\mathrm{H}^0(\mathrm{Tot}(M))=0\).

{\rm (4)} It is \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-acyclic if \(\mathrm{Tot}(M)=0\).
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->

The following assertions hold in \(

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
\).

{\rm (1)} The \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-torsion objects are closed under subobjects,
quotients, and extensions.

{\rm (2)} The \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-\(1\)-torsion
(\(\mathrm{Tot}\)-\(0\)-torsion) objects are closed under extensions and
subobjects (respectively, quotients).

{\rm (3)} \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-\(1\)-torsion objects are without finite torsion.

{\rm (4)} For \(M\in D_c^b(R)\), one has \(\mathrm{Tot}(M)=0\) if and only if
every diagonal cohomology object \(\widetilde\mathrm{H}^i(M)\) is
\(\mathrm{Tot}\)-acyclic.

    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{

\) gives
\[\begin{aligned}
    0 \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathrm{Tot}(M_{1}))
\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathrm{Tot}(M_{2}))
\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{0}(\mathrm{Tot}(M_{3}))\\
\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{1}(\mathrm{Tot}(M_{1}))
\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{1}(\mathrm{Tot}(M_{2}))
\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}^{1}(\mathrm{Tot}(M_{3}))
\longrightarrow 0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\mathrm{H}^1(\mathrm{Tot}(M))\) is torsion for every \(M\in 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{

}}              
    {\,

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);

}}           
    {\,

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);

}}

\), this
sequence gives (1) and (2). If \(M\) is
\(\mathrm{Tot}\)-\(1\)-torsion, then so is its finite-torsion subobject

(4) is precisely \Cref{Totsubquo}.

}(M,N)=0\]
for every \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-acyclic object \(N\). We denote the resulting full
subcategory by \(

<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{Mazur-Ogus vanishing}
Suppose \(M\in  
  \mathrel{\mathchoice

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}}

  } 
_{\mathrm{MO}}\). Then
\(
\mathrm{H}^{i}\!\left(R_{1}\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{R}M\right)^{j}=0
\)
if \(i+j\neq 0\), and \(M\) is without
\(\mathrm{Tot}\)-torsion.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Each \(U_0^i\) is \(\mathrm{Tot}\)-acyclic. The defining orthogonality of \(M\),
together with \Cref{Hodge numbers in degree plus minus 1}, gives the
vanishing when \(i+j=\pm1\); \Cref{Basic Vanishing}(2) gives it in all
remaining nonzero total degrees.

The spectral sequence 
\(
\mathrm{H}^{i}\!\left(R_{1}\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{R}M\right)^{j}
\Longrightarrow
\mathrm{H}^{i+j}\!\left(k\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{W}\mathrm{Tot}(M)\right)
\)
therefore concentrates \(k\otimes_W^{\mathrm{L}}\mathrm{Tot}(M)\) in degree \(0\).
The triangle
\(
\mathrm{Tot}(M)
\xrightarrow{\;p\;}
\mathrm{Tot}(M)
\longrightarrow
k\otimes^{\mathrm{L}}_{W}\mathrm{Tot}(M)
\longrightarrow
\)
then shows that \(\mathrm{Tot}(M)\) is concentrated in degree \(0\) and that
\(\mathrm{H}^0(\mathrm{Tot}(M))\) is torsion free.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{Hodge numbers in degree plus minus 1}

For all \(i,j\in\mathbb{Z}\), there are canonical isomorphisms

\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{H}^j(R_1\otimes_R^{\mathrm{L}}M)^i
 &\cong \mathrm{Hom}_{D(R)}(M,U_0[-j](1-i))^\vee\\
 &\cong \mathrm{Hom}_{D(R)}(U_0[-j-2](1-i),M).
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, for \(M\in

    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
}(M,U_0[-j](j)),\\
h^{-1-j,j}(M)&=\dim_k\mathrm{Hom}_{ 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}              
    {\,

  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.11, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}             
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.08, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}                   
  } 
}(U_0[-j-2](j+2),M).
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Regard \(R_1\) as a \((W,R)\)-bimodule, with \(W\) acting on the left.
Its graded dual \(L=\mathrm{Hom}_W(R_1,K/W)\), where
\(L^a=\mathrm{Hom}_W(R_1^{-a},K/W)\), is a graded left \(R\)-module by
\[
(r\lambda)(x)=\lambda(xr).
\]
Thus \(F,V,d\) on \(L\) are induced by right multiplication by
\(F,V,d\) on \(R_1\). The same formula defines the left \(W\)-action
on \(L\); the Hom is taken with respect to the left \(W\)-action on
\(R_1\). With this structure, \(L\cong U_0(1)\) as graded left
\(R\)-modules. The identification incorporates the sign
\(d_{U_0(1)}=-d_{U_0}\) from our grading-shift convention.
Tensor--Hom adjunction now gives
\[
\bigl(\mathrm{H}^j(R_1\otimes_R^{\mathrm{L}}M)^i\bigr)^\vee
 \cong\mathrm{Hom}_{D(R)}(M,U_0[-j](1-i)).
\]
All these spaces are finite-dimensional over \(k\), so dualizing
proves the first isomorphism.

Compatibility of duality with reduction gives
\(\mathrm{H}^{-j}(R_1\otimes_R^{\mathrm{L}}D(M))^{-i}
\cong(\mathrm{H}^j(R_1\otimes_R^{\mathrm{L}}M)^i)^\vee\).
Apply the first isomorphism to \(D(M)\), then use biduality and
\(D(U_0)\cong U_0(2)[-2]\) to obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{H}^j(R_1\otimes_R^{\mathrm{L}}M)^i
 &\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{D(R)}(D(M),U_0[j](i+1))\\
 &\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{D(R)}(U_0[-j-2](1-i),M).
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally, when \(i=1-j\) or \(i=-1-j\), the corresponding shift of
\(U_0\) lies in \( 
  \mathrel{\mathchoice
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}              
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.16, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}           
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.11, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}             
    {\, 
  \mathrel{\raisebox{-0.15ex}{\hbox{ 
  \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.08, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (1.2,1.75) -- (0.8,1.75) -- cycle;
    \draw (1.6,0)-- (0.8,1.75);
  \end{tikzpicture}}} 
}}
